sentences.text: Shri D.K.Shrivastava - Advocate for the appellant.

Ms.Nupur Dhamija - Dy.Govt. Advocate for the respondent Considered I.A.No.17420/2024, which is second application under section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant/Suresh @ Lallu.

Earlier application being I.A.No.79/2023 was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 21.8.2023.
2.

Vide impugned judgment dated 29.11.2022 passed by learned Additional Judge to the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Bareli, District Raisen in S.T.No.69/2018 the appellant/applicant has been convicted for offences under sections 450, 376 2(l) 376(2)(n) of I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 03 years, R.I. 20 years & R.I. 20 years and fine of Rs.1,000/-, Rs.2,000/- &
Rs.2000/- respectively with default stipulations.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Bareli, District Raisen
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. As per prosecution case, the prosecutrix is a mentally challenged girl.
About 08 months prior to 13.4.2018 the appellant/applicant entered the house of prosecutrix and committed sexual intercourse with her many times due to which the prosecutrix got pregnant.
Therefore, she narrated the facts to her parents.
Accordingly, F.I.R. bearing Crime No.99/2018 was registered at Police Station, Udaipura, District Raisen.
After completing the investigation charge-sheet has been filed.

The learned trial Court in S.T.No.69/2018 vide impugned judgment convicted and sentenced the 2 CRA-116-2023 appellant/applicant regarding house tress-pass and committing rape of mentally challenged girl, as mentioned above.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant/applicant submitted that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question as the family members of prosecutrix were demanding some land and when such demand was not satisfied they made false complaint.
The impugned judgment has been passed without properly appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record.
There is delay of one year in making the complaint.
the prosecutrix was aged about 19 years.
There are material omission and contradictions in the prosecution evidence.
The medical evidence does not support the prosecution case.
The appellant has remained substantial period in custody.

sentences.text: Final disposal of instant appeal would take considerable time.
Hence, prayer has been made to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant and grant of bail 5.
Learned Deputy Government Advocate for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

As per judgment of the trial Court the mother of prosecutrix in report dated 13.4.2018 itself had herself mentioned that prosecutrix is her child aged about 19 years and she is mentally challenged girl and even unable to speak properly with persons.
Some time about 10-15 days ago her daughter was suffering from stomach pain.
When she got her daughter medically checked- up she came to know that her daughter was pregnant.

On asking about the incident she mentioned the name of accused/appellant (Suresh @ Lallu) who 3 CRA-116-2023 entered into the house and committed rape upon her when other family members were not present in the house and had threatened to kill her if she discloses to anyone.
7. It is seen from the record that incident is of an year back.
There is delay of one year in making the complaint.
The prosecutrix was major aged about 19 years.

In statement of the prosecutrix (PW.1)
under section 164 Cr.P.c. she stated that there was panchayat in village in this regard.
8. In the Court the prosecutrix (PW.1) deposed against the appellant/accused.
Dr.K.K.Silawat (PW.7) has examined the accused whereas Dr.Vijay Laxmi (PW.8) has examined the prosecutrix and the medical report is Exhibit-P/4, in which, she found that there was no injury mark.
Hymen of the prosecutrix was ruptured and healed.
She was pregnant having pregnancy of 30-32 weeks.
PW.8 in her deposition has already stated that the victim told her that sexual intercourse was done by her cousin brother.
She also stated that no medical examination regarding mental status of prosecutrix was done by her.
9. In this case DNA sampling has been done and in DNA report (Exhibit-P/13) wherein it is mentioned that girl child delivered by the prosecutrix is not found to be biological daughter of the accused.

10. Looking to the over-all facts of the case, especially considering the DNA report which reflects that although girl child is biological daughter of the prosecutrix but not the biological daughter of the appellant/accused and also taking into account the custody period of the appellant from 09.5.2018 to 28.3.2019 and from the date of judgment till date, this Court is 4 CRA-116-2023 prima facie of the view that this is a fit case where jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended and appellant be granted bail.
Accordingly, I.A.No.17420/2024 is allowed.

11. It is directed that on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, the remaining part of the substantive jail sentence imposed upon appellant-Suresh @ Lallu shall remain suspended during the pendency of this case and he shall be released on bail.
Appellant shall appear before the concerned trial Court on 25.01.2025 and on all such subsequent dates, as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
